clue.text: Pay out for equipment to cover student's time off

indicators.note: the equipment word wraps around the other piece, covering it

parts.note: gear is equipment, kit

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of pay are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone pays out for kit to take on a student's break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay out' looks like spending money, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on pay alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A year out between school and university is a student's lengthy break from study.

clue.text: Grand personal attire

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
own means belonging to oneself, personal

explanation.surface: A description of someone's splendid private wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe or dress is a garment, an item of attire.

clue.text: Woman in the swim set up type of selling

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
the woman's name sits inside the word for a swim

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman in the swim of things organises a kind of sales scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' reverses the whole assembly, not just the woman's name; 'in the swim' splits as the container word plus the swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramid selling is a scheme where each seller recruits further sellers beneath them.

clue.text: New line, feminine and delicate

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for feminine in grammar

explanation.surface: A dainty new line in womenswear is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LINE with F, giving the answer with the F sitting in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elfin is small and dainty, like a fairy, so delicate in build.

clue.text: Risk asking for more time?

parts.note: a convict who breaks the law again is in effect inviting a longer prison sentence, more time inside

explanation.definitionFit: Committing a further crime courts another sentence, so it is like requesting extra jail time.

clue.text: Two daughters, one in the money, behaving dishonourably

indicators.note: the daughters and the one are placed inside the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two of them give DD
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two girls who come into a fortune start behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a man who behaves without honour, so caddish describes ungentlemanly conduct.

clue.text: Easily remembered what's full of snags, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a tune that sticks in the mind is memorable
read literally, something full of catches or hitches

explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is memorable sticks; literally, the word also means having many catches or snags.

clue.text: Uses ducking-stool, with which one lowers beam

definitions.meaning: a ducking-stool was used to plunge suspected sorceresses into water, so it dunks a sorceress
a car's control that dims the headlight beam to avoid dazzling oncoming drivers

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes dunking a sorceress; as one term it is a car headlamp control.

clue.text: Problem with prime I left to hazard

indicators.note: a problem with the letters means they are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzle involving a prime number that was left aside is a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is set before the jumbled PRIME rather than mixed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to risk or endanger it, as a verb.

clue.text: Present journal, including end of manuscript passed on

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

indicators.note: the diary word takes in the extra letter

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A journal kept today includes the final part of an old manuscript handed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes T from manuscript, which 'including' puts inside DIARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits passed on from parent to child are inherited, handed down the generations.

clue.text: Sign of cool being lost, close to answering with impudence

parts.note: in guessing games you are getting warm when near the right answer
front means cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Someone is losing their cool, getting close to answering back impudently.
explanation.walkthrough: In weather terms, cool air is replaced as this boundary passes, so cool is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map this boundary marks where advancing mild air replaces colder air.

clue.text: One set taking an exam

parts.note: examiners set the question sheet, and candidates sit it when they take the exam

explanation.definitionFit: An exam consists of a set question sheet which candidates sit, so it is the thing set.

clue.text: One of all-round experience?

parts.note: a sophisticated, worldly person, or literally someone who has been all round the globe

explanation.definitionFit: A worldly, sophisticated person has broad experience of life, as if travelled round the globe.

clue.text: For accommodation around one old university, it's astonishing

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the lodging word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: digs is informal British for lodgings
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone favours student lodgings near an ancient university, finding it amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prodigious is remarkable or enormous, so amazing in scale.

clue.text: Basic principle of one rather small change in America being admitted

indicators.note: the coin is let into the word for a small creature

parts.note: a runt is an undersized one, the smallest of a litter
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A rudimentary lesson in small American change.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a first principle or basic element of a subject.

clue.text: Element of crew brought up constant complaint -— see trouble?

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a nag is a persistent complainer, or nagging

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of see are disturbed

explanation.surface: A crew member keeps complaining about trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns NAG into GAN; 'trouble' rearranges SEE into ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: This metal is a chemical element, symbol Mn, atomic number 25.

clue.text: Contents of nasty letter revealed in probe

indicators.note: the letters come from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The contents of a poison-pen letter are exposed during an investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: This surgical instrument is a slender probe, also a fine pointed tool.

clue.text: Period of sentence finalised

parts.note: suggests a prison term completed, but means the punctuation mark that ends a written sentence

explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark, called a period in America, ends a sentence.

clue.text: Pour out depression about being hemmed in

indicators.note: the short word for about is enclosed by the depression word

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone pours out their depression about being trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant wine is to pour it gently from bottle into another vessel.

clue.text: Start to canvass more promising staff

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a rosier outlook is a more promising one

explanation.surface: Beginning to canvass staff with brighter prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's hooked staff is carried as a symbol of pastoral office.

clue.text: It's very easy to get upset

definitions.meaning: something easily done or beaten, a walkover
to ... is to topple or knock over

explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is an easy task; split in two, to push over is to topple something.

clue.text: Compete with some of party people in front of TV?

parts.note: to vie is to compete
a wing is a section of a political party

explanation.surface: Rival factions of a political party compete on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting in front of the TV is watching programmes, an activity of looking.

clue.text: Read Bible with little interest, or with a lot?

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
idly means without real effort or interest

explanation.surface: Does one read the Bible with little interest, or with plenty?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'with a lot' of interest, picking up the earlier phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something eagerly means doing it with great enthusiasm and interest.

clue.text: The world of telecommunications

parts.note: the planet seen as one small community linked by electronic media

explanation.definitionFit: This phrase describes the whole planet shrunk to a single community by electronic communication.

clue.text: River runs dry? It does

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, northern England
R is the abbreviation for runs in cricket

explanation.surface: Does a river's running water ever dry up?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'It does' dry: a clothes rack or frame on which washing is dried.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse or rack is a device that dries laundry.

clue.text: It's often baked for the head

definitions.meaning: baked haricots in tomato sauce are a common tinned food
slang for the head, as in a blow on the noggin

explanation.definitionFit: A baked legume is a familiar dish, and old slang uses the same word for the head.

clue.text: The fruit of bad round — falling back?

indicators.note: falling back means the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: evil means bad
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Bad fruit has gone round, dropping back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling back' reverses EVILO as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: This small oval stone fruit grows on Mediterranean trees.

clue.text: Discourage first person's resolve

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
mine is the first-person possessive

explanation.surface: Putting off the leading person's resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to decide firmly, so as verbs the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Witchcraft church gets miserable about?

indicators.note: the miserable word goes about the church abbreviation

parts.note: sorry means wretched, miserable
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church is made unhappy by witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is magic using evil spirits, the practice of witchcraft.

clue.text: Very good example of normal silver being shown

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
on means being shown, as a play or film

explanation.surface: An excellent specimen of everyday silver goes on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example.
